Evident Output — CLI UX v9b

Pit-of-success rendering for parallel work, plans, cancellation, effects, facts, live activity, and long-running daemons.

Live TTY — independent work starts together
Pit-of-success rules
Independent children run in parallel

branches, worktrees, and remote-tracking are siblings in a Group, so one cannot sit at “waiting” merely because another sibling is running.

Stable parent, changing child

Progress and timer stay on the parent row. One indented row shows the current item so the line can change or truncate without moving the timer.

Do not expose implementation phases

classify is hidden unless it is itself meaningful to the user. The parent reports “459 tips checked,” not an internal phase tree.

No stale Running frame

The renderer changes a visible frame at least every 100ms while work is Running, even when no application event arrives.

Dry-run — terminal output only
dry-runzq prune ~/Developer/Software-Automation-Holdings/.worktrees/eapp-system-style-contract-heading
 
✓ branches 459 checked
! kept 419 (283 checked out, 135 unpushed, 1 protected)
✓ worktrees 294 checked
! kept 292 (163 dirty, 89 unpushed, 40 ignored files)
✓ remote-tracking 4 stale refs
 
plannedbranches delete 40 local tips
plannedworktrees remove 1 worktree
plannedremote-tracking delete 4 stale origin/*
 
planned · warned
Why this is clearer
Plans are effects, not task children

Planned mutations live in one compact ledger after discovery. They are not mixed into the task hierarchy.

Routine success is compressed

The successful internal classify rows disappear. Counts remain because they explain the plan. Ordinary Facts, like on-disk size, show only under verbose (EVO_VERBOSE=1) and always appear in JSON.

Warnings explain retained work

“Kept” is important because it explains why discovered objects will not be pruned.

No fake top-level change

An empty [changed] zq record is structurally invalid and must never render.

Cancellation after some mutations already committed
zq prune --apply ~/Developer/Software-Automation-Holdings/.worktrees/eapp-system-style-contract-heading
 
- branches not started
- worktrees interrupted
✓ remote-tracking 4/4
 
changedremote-tracking deleted 4 stale origin/*
 
cancelledprune by user
! partial changes were applied before cancellation
Cancellation rules
Never imply rollback

Committed effects remain visible after cancellation. The UI explicitly says partial changes were applied.

One cancellation summary

Do not repeat a second “already mutated” sentence containing the same effect data. The changed ledger is the durable truth.

Not started ≠ interrupted

Preserve the distinction so users know which work never began and which work was in flight.

Clean success — no redundant “classify” rows
zq prune ~/Developer/Personal/zq
 
✓ branches 1 checked
! kept 1 (protected)
✓ worktrees nothing to clean
✓ remote-tracking nothing to clean
 
prune nothing to clean
Automatic verbosity
Hide zero-information children

classify 1 tip, classify 1 worktree, and classify 0 stale refs are implementation detail when the parent already communicates the result.

Keep the one useful warning

The protected branch explains why branches are not fully prunable. A lone kept item folds into its category tally instead of a separate line.

Summary appears only when useful

If every mutation category is no-op, one final “prune nothing to clean” summary is reasonable; otherwise omit it.

Dependency installation
Stable timer placement
Parent owns progress and timer

The timer stays where the eye expects it. The dependency itself appears below.

Concrete activity beats “converging”

Show urllib3 or the actual current package rather than an abstract internal state.

Partial failure — reporting follows the failed attribute
✗ write launch agent failed: permissions
- contents already satisfied
✗ permissions
error operation not permitted
path ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.acme.prod.agent.plist
mode 0644
Partial-truth rules
Plain dash for already satisfied

No exotic skip glyph. It must render reliably in ordinary terminals.

Error is a Fact of permissions

The parent tells the user what failed; the nested Fact tells them why.

Stress case — mixed live, warning, failure, and effects
Projection rules
Stable parent line

Progress and timer stay in one predictable place.

Active detail below

The current dependency/file/host gets one indented line and can change or truncate independently.

Passing Evidence stays hidden

It surfaces only when needed to explain partial truth or skipped work.

Warnings remain visually strong

The warning glyph and message both use warning emphasis.

Generic clean success + active work
Rendering rule
Completed Tasks remain landmarks

No passing Evidence rows are shown on ordinary success.

Running Task uses two lines when useful

The parent owns progress/timer; one child activity row says what is actively changing.

Already satisfied
✓ deploy production
✓ discover
✓ prepare hosts already satisfied
✓ services already satisfied
✓ write launch agent already satisfied
path ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.acme.prod.agent.plist
✓ cleanup nothing to do
Semantics
Requested state is satisfied

The Task succeeds even when its mutation was unnecessary.

Passing details remain hidden

Structured output may retain every verification result without spending terminal rows.

Long-running daemon — owner state + bounded tail
Daemon / stream rules
No fake progress bar

A daemon has no meaningful total. One owner row carries state and uptime.

Bounded INFO+ tail

The stream shows a bounded tail of INFO and WARN lines. DEBUG only appears under EVO_VERBOSE=1.

Quiet ≠ hung

A quiet timer on the owner row distinguishes “no recent output” from a frozen process. The spinner keeps animating.

Clean stop is success

A SIGTERM/^C stop resolves the owner row with a checkmark and total uptime. Exit code is 0.

Refusal is Blocked

An already-running daemon is a Blocked state, not a failure: one reason, one next step, exit code 1.

Crash loop shows the loop

Attempt count, backoff, and last exit reason — not a raw stack trace.

Non-TTY streams lines

launchd/systemd hosts get one appended line per event, never a redraw. JSONL carries every log line; the human tail stays bounded.

Pit-of-success authoring
// Siblings in a Group are independent by default.
// Evo owns the goroutines and bounded concurrency.
prune := evo.Group("prune")

branches := prune.Task("branches")
branches.Define(classifyBranches)

worktrees := prune.Task("worktrees")
worktrees.Define(classifyWorktrees)

remote := prune.Task("remote-tracking")
remote.Define(classifyRemoteTracking)

// No caller goroutines.
// No waiting state caused by declaration order.
// No manually printed "classify" progress rows.
//
// Facts discovered by each Task are model data.
// Effects are emitted separately:
//
//   [planned] branches         delete 40 local tips
//   [changed] remote-tracking  deleted 4 stale origin/*
//
// Empty or content-free Effect records are rejected;
// "[changed] zq" cannot be produced by the renderer.
Structural guarantees
Group means concurrency is available

Declaration order never silently serializes independent siblings. Use Sequence only when ordering is semantically required.

Renderer chooses verbosity

The application records Facts, progress, warnings, and Effects. It does not decide which implementation rows deserve terminal space.

Effects require meaning

A changed/planned effect needs a subject and mutation description. Content-free effects fail validation instead of becoming confusing UI.

Normative direction: independent work starts together · stable parent rows own progress/timers · current activity goes underneath · long-running streams stay bounded under one owner · implementation phases collapse automatically · Facts surface only when useful · Effects are a separate ledger · cancellation preserves committed truth · dry-run header + [planned · warned] band · daemons: ready, quiet, stopped, blocked states.
